title: A new-to-nature nitrogenase with no homology to natural nitrogenases

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 12, New nitrogenases. Target: a nitrogenase with no sequence or structural homology to the natural family that converts N2 to ammonia at rates of a similar order of magnitude to natural enzymes. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: Nonhomologous nitrogenases
page.definition: A protein converts nitrogen gas (N₂) to ammonia at a rate at least comparable in order of magnitude to that of natural nitrogenases, the enzymes that carry out biological nitrogen fixation. Neither its amino-acid sequence nor its three-dimensional structure shows detectable evidence of common ancestry with any known nitrogenase or nitrogenase-like protein.

goal.need: About 70% of ammonia goes into fertilisers. In 2020, ammonia production used 2% of global final energy and directly emitted about 450 million tonnes of CO₂, largely because it relied on fossil fuels for hydrogen and energy. An unrelated nitrogen-fixing protein would help reveal which features of natural nitrogenases are essential to the reaction. That knowledge could guide the design of catalysts for fertiliser production. Any emissions saving would depend on how the process supplies energy and electrons.

completion.title: A nonhomologous nitrogenase reaches the order of magnitude of natural nitrogenase reaction rates.
completion.criterion: A protein converts N₂ to ammonia at rates at least of a similar order of magnitude to naturally occurring nitrogenases, while falling well below sequence- and structure-similarity thresholds against all known nitrogenase and nitrogenase-like proteins. Discovery in nature, de novo design and engineering are permitted. The published acceptance conditions specify no numerical rate ratio, reference enzyme, assay conditions, similarity metric or similarity cutoff.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, published challenge acceptance conditions for problem 12, New nitrogenases, in The Millennium Problems for Biology.
completion.threshold_quote: Create a new nitrogenase that does not bear sequence or structural homology to the natural family.
completion.basis: Problem 12 requires both a rate comparison and exclusion of homology for the same protein. Its numerical boundaries remain unspecified. The 11 ± 2 turnovers reported for ArtN2ase-10 in patent Example 5 measure cumulative production. Liang and colleagues report 9.704 mg of ammonia per gram of catalyst per hour for a designed porphyrin-binding protein. Their abstract gives neither a natural-enzyme rate comparison nor a sequence and structure comparison with the known family.

milestones.title: An engineered protein–cofactor complex reduces acetylene to ethylene.
milestones.criterion: Gas chromatography detects ethylene formed from acetylene by the engineered protein–cofactor complex. Measure activity over time alongside the free cofactor under the same conditions, since the free cofactor can itself reduce acetylene.
milestones.set_by: Nitrogen-fixation community; the acetylene-reduction convention is documented by Montes-Luz and colleagues for plants and bacteria and applied to artificial proteins in the cited patent.
milestones.threshold_quote: uses gas chromatography to measure the reduction of acetylene to ethylene by nitrogenase

milestones.title: An engineered protein converts isotope-labelled nitrogen gas into isotope-labelled ammonia.
milestones.criterion: Detect ¹⁵NH₃, measured as ¹⁵NH₄⁺, after supplying ¹⁵N₂ to the engineered protein. Labelled product must exceed the background from the labelled gas and from the reaction system without protein.
milestones.set_by: Nitrogen-fixation community. Schnabel and Sattely use isotope tracing and contamination controls in biological nitrogen fixation. Patent Example 5 applies isotope tracing and protein-free controls to an artificial protein.
milestones.threshold_quote: from which we conclude that ammonia in the medium is de novo fixed from gaseous dinitrogen

milestones.title: A protein without nitrogenase sequence or structural homology catalyzes N₂ reduction to ammonia.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate N₂-to-ammonia catalysis by the candidate protein. Compare both its amino-acid sequence and its three-dimensional structure with all known nitrogenases and nitrogenase-like proteins. Neither comparison may reveal detectable homology. Problem 12 specifies no numerical similarity cutoff.
milestones.set_by: Atlas intermediate condition derived from problem 12; no separate outside acceptance test for this precompletion result was found in the challenge, programme descriptions or artificial-nitrogenase disclosures.

not_found: Problem 12 provides no numerical rate ratio, reference enzyme, assay conditions or sequence and structure similarity cutoffs.
No outside document located defines a separate precompletion test combining nitrogen reduction with exclusion of nitrogenase homology.
No peer-reviewed paper or independent replication of the reported ArtN2ase-10 nitrogen-reduction result was located.
Patent Example 5 reports triplicate assays but does not identify the statistic represented by ±2 in the ArtN2ase-10 turnover number.
No statement from a scientific society, roadmap committee or funding programme disputing the value or feasibility of problem 12 was located.

results.finding: Trp-10, one of 11 FeMoco-loaded designs tested, retained 87% of its acetylene-reduction activity after 3 hours.
results.detail: Free FeMoco started with higher activity than the engineered designs and lost activity faster. The application does not specify the number of replicates for the retention measurements.
results.quote: This mutant, termed Trp-10-HC-AA, displayed overalllower acety lene reduction activity, as well a reduced 3 hr activity retention (76%, as compared to 87% in Trp-10).

results.finding: FeMoco-loaded Trp-10, the sole construct in the reported assay, yielded a labelled ammonia signal after 10 minutes.
results.detail: The text gives neither the labelled product concentration nor the replicate count. The Figure 14 caption attributes the marked ¹⁴NH₄⁺ peaks to trace solvent contamination.
results.quote: Formation of15NHs is then confirmed by frequency selective pulse NMR analysis.

results.finding: FeMoco-loaded Trp-10, the sole construct in the reported assay, gave an ammonia signal from labelled N₂ after 10 minutes.
results.detail: The scaffold was engineered to mimic the native cofactor pocket. The reported pocket overlap measures local shape and does not establish whether the proteins share ancestry.

results.finding: Engineered NifEN P/M_S2B with NifH yielded a ¹⁵NH₄⁺ NMR doublet with a peak at 6.97 ppm after ¹⁵N₂ exposure (isotope-assay n unreported).
results.detail: The n = 3 applies to the activity assays in Figure 3. The nitrogenase-free cell control in Figure 4 measured ¹⁵N incorporation into biomass and does not establish either background for the in vitro ammonium measurement.
